propositions: The environment variable registry generator recognizes only os.environ.get, os.environ[...], and os.getenv(...), silently skipping other attribute access forms like os.environ.pop and os.environ.setdefault, causing documented keys to disappear without diagnostic.

A refactor changing os.environ.get(...) to os.environ.pop(..., None) at the same site leaves the key unregistered, violating the invariant that all environment-variable reads ship documented and producing zero exit code.

The local make lint gate does not catch stale or incomplete registry because it does not run gen_env_registry.py --check, leaving a weaker signal than CI and training contributors to trust a false negative.

The fix classifies all key-bearing os.environ attribute accesses (get, pop, setdefault, __getitem__) as registered reads, and raises UnrecognisedEnvironAccess for any access form not in the allowed sets, converting silent omission to loud failure.
The make lint target now includes gen_env_registry.py --check alongside other portable script gates, bringing local and CI verdicts into agreement on registry staleness.
